items.question: An indexer must handle chain reorganizations. What is the maximum reorg depth it has to support on Hive, and what bounds it in practice?
items.expected: Blocks at or below the last irreversible block cannot be reverted, so the practical reorg depth is head - LIB, normally a handful of blocks. There is no fixed cap: MAX_BLOCK_REORDERING = 1024 is declared but used by no code, and the fork DB window _max_size starts at 1024 and is set to head - LIB + 1 after every applied block and every accepted fast confirm, so it grows while irreversibility stalls. Undo history is bounded separately: a block that would bring head - LIB to HIVE_MAX_UNDO_HISTORY = 10,000 fails to apply with undo_database_exception (unless the check is skipped, for example for blocks at or below a configured checkpoint), so the node stops following the chain there.
forbidden: Reorgs are unbounded, any block can be reverted
Reorgs cannot exceed 21 blocks, one witness round
Hive has no reorgs because blocks are final when produced
MAX_BLOCK_REORDERING = 1024 is a hard cap on reorg depth
